Ledger text matches RFC 9110 15.5.4: "If authentication credentials were provided in the request, the server considers them insufficient to grant access. The client SHOULD NOT automatically repeat the request with the same credentials. The client MAY repeat the request with new or different credentials." The lesson (sec. 3) says more than the ledger: "a new token for the same caller changes nothing" - the RFC allows new credentials to succeed; it holds here only because the refusal is ownership and a new token carries the same sub.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: `403 Forbidden` - the status meaning "I know who you are, and I won't do this for you"; unlike `401`, which a fresh login can fix. When the refusal is about ownership, a new token for the same customer carries the same `sub`, so it changes nothing.

claim_verdicts.evidence: aspnetcore security/authorization/resource-based.md: "Attribute evaluation occurs before data binding and before execution of any method that loads a resource. Declarative authorization with an `[Authorize]` attribute doesn't suffice for resource-based authorization. Instead, the app must invoke a custom authorization method". security/authentication/index.md: "Calling `UseAuthentication` registers the middleware that uses the previously registered authentication schemes." Program.cs:70 UseAuthentication() before MapControllers.
Kind opinion, conditioned ("one way"); follows directly from claim 4, which is verified in code and live (List never returned order 3).

Live (round 2): Bearer abc.def.ghi -> GET /api/v1/orders: 'HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized', 'Www-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token"'; same token -> GET /api/v1/orders/3: 200. No token -> /orders 401, /orders/3 200. Docs security/authentication/index.md:116: challenge example "A JWT bearer scheme returning a 401 result with a `www-authenticate: bearer` header."

issues.quote: unlike `401`, which a fresh login can fix, a new token for the same caller changes nothing
issues.text: Overstated, and stronger than ledger claim 6 (which says only that re-sending the same credentials will not help). As a definition of 403 it is false in general: RFC 9110 15.5.4 says "The client MAY repeat the request with new or different credentials" - e.g. a new token for the same user with more rights can succeed. It is true only for this lesson's ownership refusal, because Đơn Hàng tokens carry just sub and email, so a new token for customer 1 has the same sub.
issues.fix: Scope it to ownership: replace with claim 6's suggested_text ("...unlike `401`, which a fresh login can fix. When the refusal is about ownership, a new token for the same customer carries the same `sub`, so it changes nothing."). Extend claim 6 text: "for an ownership refusal, a new token for the same caller has the same sub and gets the same answer" (kind behavior, source_hint: RFC 9110 15.5.4; DonHang.Api/JwtTokenService.cs:18-22@stage-1).

issues.quote: An ownership check here would do exactly that comparison after the `NotFound()` line and answer `403` when they differ
issues.text: Incomplete for this code: Get has no [Authorize], so an anonymous request has no sub to compare; adding only the comparison (int.Parse(User.FindFirstValue(Sub)!) as in List) would throw for anonymous callers instead of answering 401. The previous sentence names both gaps, but this one describes the fix as the comparison alone. Quiz q4 covers the reverse case ([Authorize] alone), not this one.
issues.fix: Append to the sentence: "— together with `[Authorize]`, so that there is always a caller to compare with." No new claim needed beyond claims 2 and 9.

issues.quote: the caller's `sub` — the claim in the token that holds the caller's customer id
issues.text: Correct (JwtTokenService.cs:20@stage-1 writes Sub = customerId.ToString(); Program.cs:31 MapInboundClaims = false keeps the name 'sub'), but no ledger claim cites where sub gets the customer id; claim 4 only says List reads it.
issues.fix: Extend claim 4's text with "; JwtTokenService writes the customer's id into sub" and add "DonHang.Api/JwtTokenService.cs:20" to its source_hint. No lesson text change.

issues.quote: If the API asked every question it should, what would it answer?
issues.text: Key a is correct given the lesson text (sec. 4: "The right response would be `403`"), and explanation c now acknowledges RFC 9110 15.5.4 ("MAY instead respond with a status code of 404"). Residual ambiguity: the stem asks what the API 'would answer', and 404 is a permitted answer, so a learner who knows the RFC is marked wrong for a valid choice.
issues.fix: Tighten the stem to ask for the status that names the failure, e.g. "...which status says what actually went wrong?" (vi: "...status nào nói đúng điều đã thất bại?"). Keep options and explanations.

issues.quote: with the caller's `sub` — the claim in the token that holds the caller's customer id.
issues.text: `sub` is now explained, but the explanation uses "claim", which is not in known_vocab, not in either prereq summary, and not defined in Core concepts. I understand the sentence only by guessing that "claim" means some kind of field. Not a blocker (the rest of the sentence carries the meaning), but I stopped here.
issues.fix: Replace "the claim in the token" with "the field in the token" (no new term needed).

issues.quote: An ownership check here would do exactly that comparison after the `NotFound()` line — together with `[Authorize]`, so that there is always a caller to compare with — and answer `403` when they differ — that code does not exist yet, so this describes what should happen, not what happens today.
issues.text: Three dashes in one sentence; I had to re-read it twice to see where the `[Authorize]` aside ends and the "does not exist yet" remark begins.
issues.fix: Split into two sentences: end the first after "answer `403` when they differ." and start a new one: "That code does not exist yet, so this describes what should happen, not what happens today."

issues.quote: You notice this when every endpoint passes authentication with the same token, yet only some of them should return what was asked for.
issues.text: The lesson's point is that the answer differs per resource (order 1 yes, order 3 no, on the same endpoint), but this sentence talks about "some" endpoints. I could not picture which endpoints are meant.
issues.fix: Make it concrete: "You notice this when customer 1's same token passes authentication for `GET /api/v1/orders/1` and `/3`, yet only order 1 should come back."
